findings.detail: The graph source applies `take the first 4096 lines` even though the generated input fixture has exactly 4096 lines (562-569). In the Unix runtime, reaching a line limit is treated as successful deliberate termination: runtime.rs around 1533-1556 returns GroupOutput with no child exit status; its Children owner kills/reaps any child not already observed exited. The graph stream executor then emits status integer 0 after the stream call returns Ok (transport.rs around 1869-1900). Thus the harness assertion that the source status payload is 0 does not establish that /bin/cat reached EOF or exited successfully. Remove the redundant take directive so the finite source completes at EOF, or add direct process-exit evidence. This is a false positive in the stated normal-source-completion oracle.

run_to_completion drains at most one event from each terminal per loop, then sleeps 2 ms while any worker remains. Two consumer terminal streams each contain 4096 events and capacity is 16; lossless backpressure prevents either consumer from finishing until the collector drains its full terminal queue. This imposes roughly 4096 poll iterations × 2 ms (~8.2 s) per sample before tail work, independent of the transport optimization. That is truthful run_to_completion end-to-end latency, but it will be dominated by the collector polling cadence and is a poor signal for transport throughput. Prefer measuring a recv_output drain loop (or explicitly scope interpretation to poll-bound run_to_completion latency); do not infer receive/emit speed from a small delta.

The report is create_new only after all runs complete. Each warmup/sample uses `?`, so one failed run or a stale preexisting report path can abort after timed work without persisting completed samples or failure diagnostics. Preflight report and fixture freshness before timing; preferably journal each completed sample and failures incrementally.
